card.adoptionSentence: The scenario assumes importers covering the 205-facility portfolio [SIM] write the clause into their supply contracts, their sellers post the bond and act on attested episodes at the scenario's rate, the stake's low bound holds, and a fixed fault stays stopped until the fault's observed end, the facility's last pass or a new fault; it assumes no new satellite and counts no clean pass as a stop.
card.costLineSentence: The ledger is cheap: USD 4.29 of Ethereum Sepolia calls per episode, USD 1,330 a year for the portfolio, USD 0.0015 per t CO₂e projected at the central action share: the cost of the records, not the work on site.
card.costSentence: Ledger cost only, not the cost of the work on site: one episode costs USD 4.29 on Ethereum Sepolia (proposeEpisode + finalize + withdraw at the stated 1 gwei and ETH/USD 2,424, measured 2026-10-22); at the portfolio's backtest rate of 309 episodes a year plus one createCovenant that is USD 1,330 a year, or USD 0.0015 per t CO₂e projected at the central action share (USD 0.00059–0.0018 across scenarios and with no recurrence). It excludes the refund-side calls and the cost of posting the bond.
card.evidenceSentence: Our two checks (MARS 'absent' label by feedback; Carbon Mapper detection rates around 437 notified sources) find no difference between answered and unanswered sources; the design cannot detect a drop smaller than 30 % of the detection rate and cannot see a partial mass cut at all, so they neither support nor bound this band.
card.floorLineSentence: Stake, not abatement: the clause puts a price on at least ~312 kt CH₄ a year across the 174 of the portfolio's 205 facilities with a quantified stake [SIM].
card.floorSentence: Stake, not abatement: at least ~312 kt CH₄/yr across the portfolio's 174 quantified facilities [SIM] (members chosen because each showed a Carbon Mapper plume MARS did not see) and ~519 kt across 428 (of the 1,122 sources MARS labels absent today — a label decided after the window), assuming what satellites saw on their passes holds between them; it is the methane the clause puts a price on, not a change in emissions.
card.headlineSentence: [PROJECTION] The clause makes each attested super-emitter a priced event the seller pays for and earns back by staying clean: one 205-facility portfolio covenant [SIM] (members chosen for a Carbon Mapper plume not in MARS, credited over each member's window from MARS's first plume there as if the covenant began then; stake quantified at 174) whose sellers act on episodes would stop ~30 kt CH₄/yr at the central 39 % action share (up to ~62 kt with no recurrence), ~0.90 Mt CO₂e/yr at GWP-100, each fix credited until the fault's observed end, the last pass or a new fault — assumptions: paper §4.
card.limitSentence: The carbon figures are a projection resting on two ASSUMPTIONs, the action share and the time share, which our own checks neither support nor bound; section 4, 'How we estimated this', states both and the checks.
card.line1Sentence: MARS outcome by response: MARS documents a per-source emission_status, but neither its committed nor its current public file carries it, so the outcome is the 'absent' label (no MARS detection over the last six months; a non-detection label, not a stop): 166 of 285 notified oil and gas sources with feedback = Yes (operator or government) against 737 of 1,227 with feedback = No, a difference of -1.8 points (95 % CI -8.2 to +4.4); +2.3 within plume-count strata; 46 and 286 sources with an undetermined label are left out.
card.line2Sentence: Event study: Carbon Mapper per-pass detection rates in the year before and after each source's first notified MARS plume (a proxy date: MARS publishes no notification date; it is also the first plume for 188 of the 437 sources used), feedback = Yes (operator or government) minus No: -0.020 (95 % CI -0.105 to +0.066) over 83 and 354 sources, -0.025 (-0.135 to +0.084) on the committed set conditioned on today's 'absent' label; every interval of the 6 specifications on both sets includes zero; minimum detectable effect 0.125 (30 % of the responders' starting rate). T0 precedes MARS's feedback tracking (November 2024) for 40 of 83 responders and 97 of 354 non-responders; the post window runs past the catalogue end for 9 and 105; responders start from a higher rate, so regression to the mean pushes toward a drop; both groups' rates rise after T0, as tasking toward expected plumes would make them.
card.methodsSentence: How we estimated this. Projected tonnes = for each facility with a quantified stake, the stake's low bound × the fixed share of its emitting time. The action share is an ASSUMPTION (32 %, 39 % central, 48 %) informed by the published share of notified incidences that were fixable faults, all fixed: when California's air regulator sent operators airborne plume detections and asked them to find the source, repair it if possible and report, operators answered 145 of 147 oil and gas incidences; 58 were faults unknown to the operator, and every one was stopped or repaired (CARB 2024); the scenarios are that share and its 95 % sampling interval (147 California incidences), which does not cover the move from a regulator's notice to a rebate under a contract; per event it is CARB's Type A share by persistence (44 % at 1 plume, n = 68; 39 % at 2 plumes, n = 28; 37 % at 3 or more plumes, n = 19), counted by incidence, as CARB publishes no emission rate per incidence. The time share is an ASSUMPTION built from the stake's own satellite passes: following Cusworth et al. 2026, a detection after a non-detection starts an event and a non-detection after a detection ends it; a fixable event is credited from its fix (its first detection plus Carbon Mapper's publication lag, median 30 days, plus the seller's response, every California Type A notification-to-mitigation delay, median 4 days) until the fault's observed end or the facility's last pass, weighted by the chance that no new fault has started (re-onset hazard 2.10 a year: 136 restarts over 64.89 event-free facility-years on the stake's own passes; the bias runs both ways: sparse passes miss restarts, and a single missed detection of a persistent source creates a false one); time before the fix, after the last pass and after a new fault is never credited. The credited days are divided by the facility's emitting days as the stake counts them (duty cycle × days to its last pass), 1.15 times the summed event lengths, so the time share errs low. Each member is credited over its window since MARS's first plume there, as if the covenant had started then: 66 % of the credit is for events containing the plume that selected the member, and a forward hold-out (members chosen before a date, credit only after it) is future work. The action share and the response delay are California's, under a regulator; 72 % of the portfolio's stake is in Turkmenistan and Venezuela, where a buyer, not a regulator, would ask. The stake assumes what satellites saw on their passes holds between them. Our two checks (MARS 'absent' label by feedback; Carbon Mapper detection rates around 437 notified sources) find no difference between answered and unanswered sources; the design cannot detect a drop smaller than 30 % of the detection rate and cannot see a partial mass cut at all, so they neither support nor bound this band. These figures are a projection of what the clause could change if adopted, not a measured reduction.
card.negativeFindingSentence: In MARS's own cross-section the answered sources are not the cleaner ones: of the 2,089 notified oil and gas sources, the 331 with feedback = Yes (operator or government) have a mean persistency of 0.140 and 16.31 plumes on average (61 persistent or frequent), against 0.083 and 5.72 (150) for the 1,513 with feedback = No; a cross-section cannot separate what a reply changes from which sources get replies (recurring sources draw more alerts). MARS publishes no notification or response date for a source, so no before/after estimate can be built from MARS alone: our event study needs a proxy date, and the projection's stop share is an ASSUMPTION informed by published figures.
card.projectionSentence: [PROJECTION] A scenario, not a measurement: if importers covering the 205-facility portfolio [SIM] wrote the clause, their sellers acted on 39 % of attested episodes (ASSUMPTION, informed by the published share of notified incidences that were fixable faults, all fixed: when California's air regulator sent operators airborne plume detections and asked them to find the source, repair it if possible and report, operators answered 145 of 147 oil and gas incidences; 58 were faults unknown to the operator, and every one was stopped or repaired (CARB 2024)), and a fix were assumed to stop its fault until the fault's observed end, the facility's last pass or a new fault (ASSUMPTION: events on the stake's own passes by Cusworth et al. 2026's definition, California's response delays; not measured after a satellite notification), ~30 kt CH₄/yr (up to ~62 kt with no recurrence) of the stake's low bound of ~312 kt (stake, not abatement) would stop, ~0.90 Mt CO₂e/yr at GWP-100 (~2.50 Mt at GWP-20) — a projection of what the clause could change if adopted, not a measured reduction.
card.scaleSentence: Scaled to the backtest set (428 facilities with a quantified stake, of the 1,122 sources MARS labels absent today — a label decided after the window), the same arithmetic gives ~62 kt CH₄ a year (up to ~97 kt with no recurrence; ~1.85 Mt CO₂e/yr at GWP-100, ~5.11 Mt at GWP-20), rising to ~76 kt (up to ~120 kt) at the top of the interval for the share of episodes sellers act on (48 %).
card.scenariosSentence: [PROJECTION] By action scenario (ASSUMPTION), portfolio [SIM], of the stake's low bound of ~312 kt (stake, not abatement): 32 % acted on → ~25 kt CH₄/yr (up to ~51 kt with no recurrence), 39 % acted on → ~30 kt CH₄/yr (up to ~62 kt with no recurrence), 48 % acted on → ~37 kt CH₄/yr (up to ~76 kt with no recurrence); every value is in data/derived/projection.json — a projection of what the clause could change if adopted, not a measured reduction.
card.widerSetSentence: [PROJECTION] Over all 428 facilities with a quantified stake (of the 1,122 sources MARS labels absent today — a label decided after the window), the same assumptions (ASSUMPTION) give ~62 kt CH₄/yr (up to ~97 kt with no recurrence) at the central action share of the stake's low bound of ~519 kt (stake, not abatement), ~1.85 Mt CO₂e/yr at GWP-100 — a projection of what the clause could change if adopted, not a measured reduction.

line1.outcome: persistency_category == 'absent' (no MARS detection over the last six months; a non-detection label, not a confirmed stop); emission_status is documented by MARS but absent from the data
line1.population: notified oil and gas sources with feedback Yes (operator or government) or No and a determined persistency category ('Undetermined' left out, counted per group)

allNotified.coverage: every notified oil and gas source with feedback Yes or No: cm_timelines.json plus cm_timelines_notified.json

joinNeighbourhood.coverage: cm_timelines.json only: the neighbourhood of the sources MARS labels absent today, a label decided after the window

line2.mdeNote: minimum detectable effect = (z at the confidence level + z at the power) x the bootstrap standard error of the difference; it is a detection-rate difference and says nothing about a partial cut in emitted mass
line2.outcome: Carbon Mapper per-pass detection rate (a pass with any plume of the owned sources counts as a detection), mean over sources, before vs after the proxy notification date
line2.population: notified oil and gas MARS sources with feedback Yes (operator or government) or No; Carbon Mapper sources owned by the nearest notified source within the join radius
threats: T0 is a proxy (the first notified plume), not the notification or the response date; for the sources used, `proxyDatesAgree` counts where the first plume is the first notified one
feedback is tracked only for sources whose latest plume is from November 2024 or later (MARS definitions); `t0BeforeFeedbackTracking` counts used sources whose T0 is earlier
post windows that run past the catalogue end are shorter (`postWindowTruncated`), and more so for one group
Carbon Mapper passes are partly tasked toward expected plumes, more so after Tanager's launch: both groups' rates rise after T0
responders start from a higher detection rate: regression to the mean pushes the difference toward a drop
non-responders may repair without replying, and a reply may come after the window: both push the difference toward zero
detection is binary above an instrument floor: a partial cut in emitted mass is invisible to it, so the design cannot bound a mass share

formula: kt CH4/yr = sum over quantified facilities of stake low bound x the fixed share of its emitting time (action share by plume count x credited days / emitting days)

bootstrap.rule: members resampled with replacement, as many as there are, each draw re-measuring the re-onset hazard on the drawn members' passes up to D and recomputing the central figure (central action share) and its share of the drawn credited members' stake; percentile interval. Draws, seed and confidence are the projection's existing bootstrap design (projection_sources.json parameters.evidence)

card.comparisonSentence: Credited over each member's whole window instead, the same model gives ~30 kt CH₄/yr for the portfolio covenant set v3, 66 % of it on events containing the plume that selected the member; the forward hold-out credits none.
card.costSentence: Ledger cost only, not the cost of the work on site: on the forward basis the 220 members had 129 episodes from 2025-09-12 to 2026-09-13; at USD 4.29 an episode plus one createCovenant that is USD 555 a year, or USD 0.0055 per t CO₂e projected at the central action share (USD 0.0038–0.0067 across scenarios and with no recurrence); credited over each member's whole window instead, the portfolio covenant set v3 costs USD 0.0015 per t CO₂e.
card.hazardSentence: In the forward hold-out the re-onset hazard is measured on the members' own passes up to 2025-09-12 only, 1.01 a year: 75 restarts over 74.05 event-free facility-years (over each member's whole window, 2.10 a year: 136 restarts over 64.89); each fix is credited until the fault's observed end, the last pass on or before 2026-09-13 or a new fault.
card.headlineSentence: [PROJECTION] Pre-registered forward hold-out: a 220-facility portfolio covenant [SIM], chosen with Carbon Mapper plumes published before 2025-09-12 at sources MARS had not seen for six months and lists as absent today, and credited only for faults first detected after that date up to 2026-09-13, would stop ~3.4 kt CH₄/yr at the central 39 % action share (95 % member bootstrap ~0.9–6.5 kt; ~2.8–5.0 kt across action and recurrence scenarios), ~0.10 Mt CO₂e/yr at GWP-100, none of it on the plume that selected a member — assumptions: paper §4.
card.intervalSentence: Resampling the members (2,000 draws, the re-onset hazard re-measured in each) puts the central figure between ~0.9 and ~6.5 kt CH₄/yr (95 % interval).
card.limitsSentence: The forward members come from today's MARS targets (notified and labelled absent today; 135 other notified oil and gas sources MARS had not seen for six months on 2025-09-12 lie outside them because their Carbon Mapper plume rows are not committed), and both catalogues are read as they stand today: MARS rows and Carbon Mapper passes without a detection carry no publication date, and 53 detections dated up to 2025-09-12 were published only on or after it (without them, ~3.3 kt); today's 'absent' label is decided inside the credit window; credit ending before it (to 2026-03-11) gives ~0.6 kt; a twelve-month credit window from 2025-03-12 to 2026-03-11, also before the label window, gives ~1.61 kt (1.87 % of stake, against 0.85 % for the credit ending before the label and 4.01 % over the full window), but the control differs by period and members as well as length, so it does not separate the window's length from the label.
card.rollingSentence: At three more origins registered after this result, with overlapping credit windows, the share is 2.6–2.9 %.
card.stakeSentence: Stake, not abatement: ~84 kt CH₄/yr across the 115 members with a stake known on 2025-09-12 and a satellite pass after it; the projection credits 4.0 % of it (3.4 % of the ~99 kt stake of all 143 quantified members).

card.headlineSentence: [PROJECTION] The clause turns each attested super-emitter into a priced event the seller pays for and can earn back by staying clean: one 205-facility portfolio covenant [SIM] (members chosen because each showed a Carbon Mapper plume MARS did not see; stake quantified at 174: 4 own no Carbon Mapper source, 27 no quantified plume in the window) whose sellers act on episodes would stop ~18–~73 kt CH₄/yr at the central 39 % action share, from one repair round net of new faults (Ravikumar 2020: 22 %) to every fix holding all year; ~0.53–2.17 Mt CO₂e/yr at GWP-100 — assumptions: paper §4.
card.limitSentence: The carbon figures are a projection resting on two ASSUMPTIONs, the action share and the stop share, which our own checks neither support nor bound; section 4, 'How we estimated this', states both and the checks.
card.line1Sentence: MARS outcome by response: MARS documents a per-source emission_status, but neither its committed nor its current public file carries it, so the outcome is the 'absent' label (no MARS detection over the last six months; a non-detection label, not a stop): 166 of 285 notified oil and gas sources with feedback = Yes (operator or government) against 737 of 1,227 with feedback = No, a difference of -1.8 points (95 % CI -8.2 to +4.4); +2.3 within plume-count strata; 46 and 286 sources with an undetermined label are left out.
card.line2Sentence: Event study: Carbon Mapper per-pass detection rates in the year before and after each source's first notified MARS plume (a proxy date: MARS publishes no notification date; it is also the first plume for 188 of the 437 sources used), feedback = Yes (operator or government) minus No: -0.020 (95 % CI -0.105 to +0.066) over 83 and 354 sources, -0.025 (-0.135 to +0.084) on the committed set conditioned on today's 'absent' label; every interval of the 6 specifications on both sets includes zero; minimum detectable effect 0.125 (30 % of the responders' starting rate). T0 precedes MARS's feedback tracking (November 2024) for 40 of 83 responders and 97 of 354 non-responders; the post window runs past the catalogue end for 9 and 105; responders start from a higher rate, so regression to the mean pushes toward a drop; both groups' rates rise after T0, as tasking toward expected plumes would make them.
card.methodsSentence: How we estimated this. Projected tonnes = the stake's low bound × the share of attested episodes sellers act on, each a fixable fault fixed, above today's 13 % reply rate (a reply, not an action) to MARS alerts (UNEP via UN News 2026), which bounds the fixes replies already drive, × the share of a fixed source's yearly emissions that stops. The action share is an ASSUMPTION (32 %, 39 % central, 48 %) informed by the published share of notified incidences that were fixable faults, all fixed: when California's air regulator sent operators airborne plume detections and asked them to find the source, repair it if possible and report, operators answered 145 of 147 oil and gas incidences; 58 were faults unknown to the operator, and every one was stopped or repaired (CARB 2024); the scenarios are that share and its 95 % sampling interval (147 California incidences), which does not cover the move from a regulator's notice to a rebate under a contract; it counts incidences, as CARB publishes no emission rate per incidence. The stop share is an ASSUMPTION with two ends from Ravikumar et al. 2020's re-survey of repaired leaks at Alberta facilities 6 to 13 months later: 22 % at the low end, the fall in leak emissions after one repair round net of new leaks; 90 % at the high end, the share of the found leaks' emissions that was fixed (a repair rate), with fixed leaks not re-appearing, read as every fix holding all year; neither end was measured after a satellite notification. Time is not yet modelled: the delay from detection to repair, how long an event lasts, new faults and sources that stop on their own are not separated, and the range spans them, so there is no central tonnage. The stake assumes what satellites saw on their passes holds between them. Our two checks (MARS 'absent' label by feedback; Carbon Mapper detection rates around 437 notified sources) find no difference between answered and unanswered sources; the design cannot detect a drop smaller than 30 % of the detection rate and cannot see a partial mass cut at all, so they neither support nor bound this band. These figures are a projection of what the clause could change if adopted, not a measured reduction.
card.negativeFindingSentence: In MARS's own cross-section the answered sources are not the cleaner ones: of the 2,089 notified oil and gas sources, the 331 with feedback = Yes (operator or government) have a mean persistency of 0.140 and 16.31 plumes on average (61 persistent or frequent), against 0.083 and 5.72 (150) for the 1,513 with feedback = No; a cross-section cannot separate what a reply changes from which sources get replies (recurring sources draw more alerts). MARS publishes no notification or response date for a source, so no before/after estimate can be built from MARS alone: our event study needs a proxy date, and the projection's stop share is an ASSUMPTION informed by published figures.
card.projectionSentence: [PROJECTION] A scenario, not a measurement: if importers covering the 205-facility portfolio [SIM] wrote the clause, their sellers acted on 39 % of attested episodes (ASSUMPTION, informed by the published share of notified incidences that were fixable faults, all fixed: when California's air regulator sent operators airborne plume detections and asked them to find the source, repair it if possible and report, operators answered 145 of 147 oil and gas incidences; 58 were faults unknown to the operator, and every one was stopped or repaired (CARB 2024); today's MARS reply rate is 13 %, UNEP via UN News 2026), and a fixed source were assumed to stop 22 %–90 % of its yearly emissions (ASSUMPTION, two ends informed by Ravikumar et al. 2020's re-survey of repaired leaks: one repair round net of new faults, every fix holding all year; neither measured after a satellite notification), ~18–~73 kt CH₄/yr of the stake's low bound of ~312 kt (stake, not abatement) would stop, ~0.53–2.17 Mt CO₂e/yr at GWP-100 (~1.47–6.02 Mt at GWP-20), with no central value until time is modelled, counting only action above the 13 % reply rate — a projection of what the clause could change if adopted, not a measured reduction.
card.scaleSentence: Scaled to the backtest set (428 facilities with a quantified stake, of the 1,122 sources MARS labels absent today — a label decided after the window), the same arithmetic gives ~30–~121 kt CH₄ a year (~0.89–3.62 Mt CO₂e/yr at GWP-100, ~2.45–10.02 Mt at GWP-20), rising to ~40–~164 kt (~1.19–4.87 Mt CO₂e/yr at GWP-100) at the top of the interval for the share of episodes sellers act on (48 %).
card.scenariosSentence: [PROJECTION] By action scenario (ASSUMPTION), portfolio [SIM], over the two ends of the stop share, of the stake's low bound of ~312 kt (stake, not abatement): 32 % acted on → ~13–~53 kt CH₄/yr (~0.39–1.59 Mt CO₂e at GWP-100), 39 % acted on → ~18–~73 kt CH₄/yr (~0.53–2.17 Mt CO₂e at GWP-100), 48 % acted on → ~24–~98 kt CH₄/yr (~0.71–2.93 Mt CO₂e at GWP-100); every edge is in data/derived/projection.json — a projection of what the clause could change if adopted, not a measured reduction.
card.widerSetSentence: [PROJECTION] Over all 428 facilities with a quantified stake (of the 1,122 sources MARS labels absent today — a label decided after the window), the same assumptions (ASSUMPTION) give ~30–~121 kt CH₄/yr at the central action share of the stake's low bound of ~519 kt (stake, not abatement), ~0.89–3.62 Mt CO₂e/yr at GWP-100 — a projection of what the clause could change if adopted, not a measured reduction.

model.criterion: Each emission is removed by exactly one factor, and each factor is measured on the population it multiplies. The stake is the mass of plume-detected emissions at a contracted source, whatever their cause, and an attested episode prices any such detection; so (1) the factor that removes what a repair cannot touch must be measured on plume-detected emissions after a notification, and (2) the factor after it must be measured on repaired faults only, so that it removes nothing the first factor already removed and credits nothing a repair did not cause. (3) The second factor's time base is a year at the stake's sources: it must say what share of a fixed source's yearly emissions stops, counting new faults, the emissions before detection and during repair, and sources that stop on their own. The option whose factors meet (1), (2) and (3) is chosen. If none meets (3), the projection is a range over the options that meet (1) and (2), with no single central tonnage, until the time factor is built (board T4c).

baselineResponseShare.note: Today's baseline, without the clause: the most recent published share of UNEP IMEO MARS alerts that received a response (13 % in UN News, July 2026; 12 % in the year to October 2025). A response is detailed information on the event, not an action and not a confirmed stop; it is the nearest published analogue to a seller acting on an attested episode. The projection counts only the action share above it: it bounds the reply-driven fixes, not sources that stop on their own (natural stops), which the interim range spans. Subtracting a reply rate from an outcome rate is conservative: MARS outcomes are far rarer than replies (more than 40 verified repairs after more than 5,000 alerts), so the share of reply-driven fixes that would happen anyway is smaller than the baseline subtracted; it says nothing about sources that stop on their own.

rule.text: the most recent published MARS response share: of the candidates below, the source with the latest date; the value is the per-cent figure in its quote. pipeline/projection.py re-reads it and refuses to run if the value differs.

baselineResponseShare.unit: share of MARS alerts that received a response (the nearest published analogue to acting on an episode)

ceasedShare.note: ASSUMPTION, the two ends of an interim range informed by the one published re-survey of repaired leaks we found: Ravikumar et al. 2020 surveyed 36 Alberta facilities from the ground and re-surveyed 8 of them 6 to 13 months later. Low end: fugitive emissions fell only 22 % after one repair round, because of new leaks (one round, net of new faults). High end: 93 % of the leaks, carrying 90 % of the fugitive emissions found, were fixed before the re-survey and the fixed ones did not re-appear, read as every fix holding all year; 0.90 is a repair rate, used only as this upper-end assumption. Time is not yet modelled: the delay from detection to repair, how long an event lasts, new faults and sources that stop on their own are spanned by the range, not separated (board T4c). Not measured after a satellite notification, on super-emitters, or over a full year; one operator's sites. The study's 44 % fall in total emissions is not used: it is measured on all of a facility's emissions and is mostly a vent change the paper reports 'despite near-zero repair' (model.options.a). Our own checks (projection_evidence.py) neither support nor bound it.

responseScenarios.note: ASSUMPTION, informed by the published share of notified incidences that were fixable faults, all fixed. California's air regulator (CARB) sent operators airborne plume detections and asked them to find the source, repair it if possible and report; operators answered nearly every oil and gas incidence, and the Type A ones (a fault unknown to the operator before the notice) were every one stopped or repaired; the rule above turns the oil and gas rows into the scenarios. In the model (model.factors.r) this is the only factor that removes emissions a repair cannot touch (Type B allowed operation, Type C maintenance, not found, no response). Counted by incidence: CARB publishes no emission rate per incidence (model.rules.massWeighting). Not observed under the clause: a seller who pays a rebate on every attested episode is not an operator answering a regulator, aerial notices are not satellite ones, and California is one jurisdiction; the interval is sampling uncertainty only and does not cover that move. The move can err either way: Type B emissions (normal operation) were classified as allowable, while under the clause each one still costs the seller a rebate; a contract counterparty has less reach than a regulator. Voluntary satellite alerts sit far lower (MARS: responses, not actions, to 13 % of alerts and more than 40 verified repairs after more than 5,000 alerts), which is why only the share above today's MARS response share counts.

incidences.text: CARB Appendix Tables A1 (2021) and A2 (2023), oil and gas rows, one per incidence, committed as aggregates (counts by year, outcome and plume count, the join-key count, the Type A delays); make fetch-published rebuilds the rows locally and checks that they reproduce the aggregates. pipeline/projection.py refuses to run unless their outcome counts equal the 2021 and 2023 rows above, and uses them for the plume-weighted sensitivity row, the join-key count and the time factor's delays and plume classes (model.t4c, model.t4d). They carry no emission rate, so r stays counted by incidence (model.rules.massWeighting).

weighting.decision: Mass weighting needs an emission rate per incidence. If a published per-incidence rate exists (CARB's own tables first, a Carbon Mapper plume rate joined by an identifier second), r is the mass-weighted share of 2021 and 2023 and its interval a percentile bootstrap over incidences (seed and draws written before running). If none exists, r stays counted by incidence, the per-incidence rows are committed with their source, SHA-256 and readOn and re-checked against Table 3, and the gap and what would close it are written down. Read on 2026-10-20: CARB Appendix Tables A1 (2021) and A2 (2023) give, per incidence, sector, outcome, earliest plume date, number of plumes and dates, but no emission rate, location or plume identifier; Carbon Mapper's 2023 plume list (CARB contract 22RD001, Appendix B) gives rates and locations but no incidence identifier, and a date-and-plume-count key identifies the incidence for few rows. So r stays counted by incidence.
